region.name: Piedmont Triad
region.intro: Greensboro addresses split at Elm St (east/west) and Market St (north/south). Learn those two, then the Urban Loop and three interstates — I-40 west to Winston-Salem, I-85 southwest past High Point, I-73 north–south past PTI — and the whole Triad snaps into place.

origin.label: Elm & Market
origin.note: Greensboro addresses flip from North to South at Market St, and from East to West at Elm St — so "N Elm" or "W Market" already tells you which side of downtown you're on.

corridors.name: I-40
corridors.desc: The Triad's east–west spine: Winston-Salem → Kernersville → Greensboro. Just east of Greensboro (near McLeansville) it merges with I-85 and the two run together toward Burlington and Durham.

corridors.name: I-85
corridors.desc: Charlotte ↔ Durham. Passes south of High Point (Archdale/Thomasville), bypasses Greensboro on the southern Urban Loop, then joins I-40 east to Burlington.

corridors.name: I-73
corridors.desc: North–south through west Greensboro along the western Urban Loop past PTI Airport — north toward Summerfield (US 220), south toward Asheboro.

corridors.name: I-74
corridors.desc: Runs up High Point's east side from I-73/I-85 to I-40, and on as the Winston-Salem Northern Beltway around the east side of Winston-Salem.

corridors.name: Urban Loop
corridors.desc: The Greensboro Urban Loop rings the city. Its arcs carry different shields: I-73 on the west, I-85 on the south, I-785 and I-840 across the north and east.

corridors.name: US 29 / O'Henry Blvd
corridors.desc: O'Henry Blvd — Greensboro's east-side freeway from I-40/85 north past the Urban Loop toward Reidsville and Danville.

corridors.name: Wendover Ave
corridors.desc: Greensboro's busiest corridor: an expressway (US 70/220) curving from High Point and Jamestown past the big-box strips at I-40, across the middle of the city, then east toward Burlington.

corridors.name: Bryan Blvd
corridors.desc: Expressway from central Greensboro northwest to PTI Airport — the airport shortcut.

corridors.name: NC 68 / Eastchester Dr
corridors.desc: High Point's north–south spine: Eastchester Dr through north High Point, then a freeway past PTI Airport toward Oak Ridge.

corridors.name: US 52
corridors.desc: John Gold Memorial Expressway — Winston-Salem's north–south freeway, toward Mount Airy to the north and (with I-285) Lexington to the south.

corridors.name: I-285
corridors.desc: Short interstate from I-85 at Lexington north into Winston-Salem, sharing pavement with US 52.

corridors.name: Salem Pkwy
corridors.desc: The freeway through downtown Winston-Salem (US 421) — formerly "Business 40", rebuilt and renamed in 2020.

corridors.name: Market St
corridors.desc: The north/south ZERO LINE of Greensboro addresses — "N Elm" becomes "S Elm" here. West Market runs past the UNCG side of town; East Market runs past NC A&T.

corridors.name: Elm St
corridors.desc: The east/west ZERO LINE — "W Market" becomes "E Market" at Elm. Downtown's main street; continues south as Elm-Eugene St toward I-85.

corridors.name: Friendly Ave
corridors.desc: Leafy west-side artery from downtown past Friendly Center out toward Guilford College.

corridors.name: Battleground Ave
corridors.desc: The US 220 diagonal: northwest from downtown past Lawndale-area shopping to Guilford Courthouse battlefield, then expressway toward Summerfield.

corridors.name: Lawndale Dr
corridors.desc: North-central shopping corridor between Battleground Ave and Elm St, heading north toward Lake Brandt.

corridors.name: Church St
corridors.desc: Runs north from downtown, parallel to Elm, through the old north-side neighborhoods toward Cone Blvd.

corridors.name: Summit Ave
corridors.desc: Northeast diagonal out of downtown, passing near Moses Cone Hospital toward the northeast Urban Loop.

corridors.name: Cone Blvd
corridors.desc: North Greensboro crosstown linking Battleground, Lawndale, Elm and Church east toward US 29.

corridors.name: Pisgah Church Rd
corridors.desc: Crosstown a mile or so north of Cone Blvd, linking the Lawndale/Battleground area to N Elm St.

corridors.name: New Garden Rd
corridors.desc: Northwest arterial linking the Guilford College area to Battleground Ave near the battlefield.

corridors.name: Holden Rd
corridors.desc: West-side north–south route between the I-40 / Gate City Blvd area and Friendly Ave.

corridors.name: Guilford College Rd
corridors.desc: Far-west north–south arterial past Guilford College, south toward Jamestown.

corridors.name: Gate City Blvd
corridors.desc: Formerly Lee St and High Point Rd — southwest from downtown past the Coliseum and Four Seasons toward Jamestown and High Point.

corridors.name: Spring Garden St
corridors.desc: UNCG's main street, running west from downtown along the campus.

corridors.name: Randleman Rd
corridors.desc: South Greensboro route from downtown toward I-85 and the town of Randleman.

corridors.name: Main St (High Point)
corridors.desc: High Point's north–south spine through downtown and the furniture-market showroom district.

corridors.name: Silas Creek Pkwy
corridors.desc: Parkway arcing around Winston-Salem's west side, past Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center toward Hanes Mall.

corridors.name: Stratford Rd
corridors.desc: Southwest shopping corridor from the Silas Creek area out to Hanes Mall.

corridors.name: Peters Creek Pkwy
corridors.desc: Main north–south commercial route on Winston-Salem's south side, from downtown across I-40.

corridors.name: University Pkwy (W-S)
corridors.desc: North from downtown past Joel Coliseum and near Wake Forest University toward US 52 north.

corridors.name: Reynolda Rd
corridors.desc: Northwest route out of downtown past Reynolda House and Wake Forest toward Yadkinville.

corridors.name: Main St (W-S)
corridors.desc: Downtown Winston-Salem's spine, running south through Old Salem.

districts.name: Downtown Greensboro
districts.why: Elm & Market, LeBauer Park, the Tanger Center and the ballpark — and the origin of every Greensboro address.

districts.name: Fisher Park
districts.why: Historic park-side neighborhood just north of downtown.

districts.name: Irving Park
districts.why: Established north-side neighborhood around Greensboro Country Club, between Elm and Battleground.

districts.name: UNCG / College Hill
districts.why: UNCG campus and the College Hill historic district, west of downtown along Spring Garden St.

districts.name: NC A&T
districts.why: North Carolina A&T State University — the largest HBCU in the country — just east of downtown on E Market.

districts.name: Coliseum area
districts.why: Greensboro Coliseum Complex on Gate City Blvd — the ACC Tournament's longtime home.

districts.name: Friendly Center
districts.why: Greensboro's main open-air shopping district, at Friendly Ave & Wendover.

districts.name: Four Seasons / Koury
districts.why: Four Seasons Town Centre and the Koury Convention Center, by I-40 & Gate City Blvd.

districts.name: Guilford College
districts.why: Quaker college neighborhood on Greensboro's west side.

districts.name: Sedgefield
districts.why: Golf-course neighborhood in southwest Greensboro, near the High Point line.

districts.name: PTI Airport
districts.why: Piedmont Triad International — reached by Bryan Blvd, I-73 or NC 68; a FedEx hub.

districts.name: Greensboro
districts.why: Guilford County seat and the Triad's largest city, ringed by the Urban Loop.

districts.name: High Point
districts.why: "Home Furnishings Capital of the World" — hosts the twice-yearly High Point Market.

districts.name: Winston-Salem
districts.why: Forsyth County seat; once tobacco and textiles, now anchored by Wake Forest and its medical center.

districts.name: Burlington
districts.why: Alamance County's largest city, on I-40/85 east of Greensboro.

districts.name: Jamestown
districts.why: Small town between Greensboro and High Point; home to GTCC's main campus.

districts.name: Kernersville
districts.why: "Heart of the Triad" — on I-40 midway between Greensboro and Winston-Salem.

districts.name: Oak Ridge
districts.why: Semi-rural town northwest of PTI along NC 68.

districts.name: Summerfield
districts.why: Town north of Greensboro along US 220.

districts.name: Stokesdale
districts.why: Northwest Guilford town toward Belews Lake.

districts.name: Pleasant Garden
districts.why: Rural town just south of Greensboro.

districts.name: Gibsonville
districts.why: Small town straddling the Guilford/Alamance county line.

districts.name: Elon
districts.why: Home of Elon University, just west of Burlington.

districts.name: Whitsett
districts.why: Small town on I-40/85 between Greensboro and Burlington.

districts.name: Sedalia
districts.why: Small town east of Greensboro along US 70.

districts.name: Archdale
districts.why: High Point's southern neighbor on I-85 / I-74.

districts.name: Thomasville
districts.why: Davidson County's "Chair City", on I-85 southwest of High Point.

districts.name: Clemmons
districts.why: Village southwest of Winston-Salem where I-40 crosses toward the Yadkin River.

districts.name: Lewisville
districts.why: Town just west of Winston-Salem.

districts.name: Walkertown
districts.why: Town northeast of Winston-Salem.

districts.name: Rural Hall
districts.why: Town north of Winston-Salem along US 52.
